title: $g^*$ is symmetric monoidal
statement:
The strong monoidal functor $g^*$ of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal] is compatible
with the symmetries: it is a symmetric monoidal functor. In particular $g^*$ sends
commutative ring objects to commutative ring objects.

proof.text: Put $L=g^*$, $R=g_*$, $\mathcal C=\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$ and $\mathcal D=\Sh(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$. Use the natural bijection $\Phi$ and unit $\eta$ of [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction] and lax tensor map $m$ of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-lax-monoidal]. For $F,G\in\mathcal C$ put $a_{F,G}=m_{LF,LG}\circ(\eta_F\otimes\eta_G)$. By [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal], $\delta_{F,G}=\Phi^{-1}(a_{F,G})$ is the specified invertible oplax comparison; put $\gamma_{F,G}=\delta_{F,G}^{-1}$. Apply [lem-sfb-unit-tensor-braiding] with $X=F,Y=G,P=LF,Q=LG,u=\eta_F,v=\eta_G$. Its braided hypothesis is supplied by the lax symmetry compatibility of $R$. It gives $R(\beta^{\mathcal D}_{LF,LG})\circ a_{F,G}=a_{G,F}\circ\beta^{\mathcal C}_{F,G}$.

source.place: first paragraph, composite and braiding calculation

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-adjunction-transpose-square] with $X'=F\otimes G$, $X=G\otimes F$, $Y=LF\otimes LG$, $Y'=LG\otimes LF$, $f=\beta^{\mathcal C}_{F,G}$, $s=a_{G,F}$, $t=a_{F,G}$ and $k=\beta^{\mathcal D}_{LF,LG}$. Step 1 is its right-hand equality (with the sides exchanged). Its left-hand equality therefore gives $\delta_{G,F}\circ L(\beta^{\mathcal C}_{F,G})=\beta^{\mathcal D}_{LF,LG}\circ\delta_{F,G}$.

source.place: first paragraph, transposing back and displayed identity

proof.text: Compose this identity on the left with $\gamma_{G,F}$ and on the right with $\gamma_{F,G}$. Cancelling inverse pairs, as allowed by [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal], gives $L(\beta^{\mathcal C}_{F,G})\circ\gamma_{F,G}=\gamma_{G,F}\circ\beta^{\mathcal D}_{LF,LG}$. This is the symmetry compatibility of the specified strong monoidal structure on $L$.

For a commutative ring object $(B,\rho,e)$, [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport], clauses 1 and 2, gives the ring object $LB$ with multiplication $\rho_L=L(\rho)\circ\gamma_{B,B}$ and unit $e_L=L(e)\circ j$, where $j:\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}\to L\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}$ is the inverse oplax unit comparison. The braided hypothesis is step 3. Explicitly, $\rho_L\circ\beta^{\mathcal D}_{LB,LB}=L(\rho)\circ L(\beta^{\mathcal C}_{B,B})\circ\gamma_{B,B}=L(\rho\circ\beta^{\mathcal C}_{B,B})\circ\gamma_{B,B}=\rho_L$, since $\rho\circ\beta^{\mathcal C}_{B,B}=\rho$. Thus the transported ring object is commutative.
